headline: Record orders and margins power a blowout quarter

kpis.label: Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash

summary_short: Keysight delivered the strongest quarter in company history: revenue rose 31.5% y/y to $1,717M on record orders of $2,051M (+55.9% y/y), with GAAP net income up 35.8% y/y to $349M ($2.02 diluted EPS) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.87 (+68.8% y/y).
summary_long: CSG revenue grew 35% y/y on 40% growth in commercial communications and 24% in aerospace/defense/government; EISG grew 24% on broad-based automotive, energy, general-electronics, and semiconductor demand. Segment operating margins expanded sharply (CSG to 33% from 26%; EISG to 33% from 23%), driving operating income up 96.6% y/y to $407M and net income up 35.8% to $349M. A one-time IEEPA tariff ruling added a $100M receivable and a net benefit to cost of sales this quarter, aiding gross-margin comparability. Free cash flow rose 3.3% y/y to $472M; cash, equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $2.43B. Keysight raised its full-year outlook and guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to $1.730-1.750B (~29% y/y growth) and non-GAAP EPS to $2.43-$2.49.

drivers.explanation: CSG revenue rose 35% y/y (40% growth in commercial communications, 24% in aerospace/defense/government); EISG rose 24% y/y on double-digit growth across automotive/energy, general electronics, and semiconductor end markets.
Not broken out by driver in the release; management's overall commentary attributes the record $2.05B in orders to accelerating demand across the same end markets driving segment revenue growth.
CSG operating margin expanded to 33% from 26% and EISG to 33% from 23% y/y per segment disclosures, so operating income grew far faster than the 31.5% revenue increase.
Tracks the operating-income gain; partly offset by higher interest expense ($25M vs $20M) and a swing in other income/expense ($18M vs $112M a year ago), while the effective tax rate eased slightly.
Tracks the net-income increase; basic weighted shares were roughly flat (171M vs 172M y/y).
Tracks the net-income increase; diluted weighted shares were flat at 173M y/y.
GAAP EPS growth plus normal non-GAAP add-backs (amortization $73M, stock comp $58M); acquisition/integration items swung from a $74M net benefit a year ago to a $31M expense, a partial offset.
Cost of products and services rose only 9.6% y/y ($539M vs $492M) versus 31.5% revenue growth; cost of sales also received a $93M one-time benefit from the IEEPA tariff-refund ruling this quarter.
Tracks the net-income, interest-expense, and tax-provision components described above (EBIT = net income + interest expense + tax provision).
Operating cash flow rose to $501M from $484M while capex was roughly flat ($29M vs $27M), per the company's own free-cash-flow reconciliation table.

CEO Satish Dhanasekaran called it the strongest quarter in company history, capping a record first half with all-time highs in orders, revenue, EPS, and free cash flow, and cited accelerating demand and prior strategic investments; full-year outlook raised.
